sources.subject: General rain-garden routing and underdrain distinction
sources.operation: Official educational mechanism and maintenance guidance; no site measurement
sources.locator: How does a rain garden work? / Why would I need an underdrain? / What maintenance is needed; independent text lines 16–27
sources.conditions: A configured underdrain can return filtered water to a storm sewer; without one water can enter native soil. One-to-two-day drainage is a general statement, not this site's criterion.
sources.unit: day; neither site dimensions nor published removal percentages adopted
sources.type: Educational guidance; underdrained versus non-underdrained systems
sources.exceptions: Unknown site configuration and jurisdiction; no local benefit inferred

sources.operation: MPCA overview; water-quantity treatment and surrounding permit context
sources.locator: Water quantity treatment; text lines 56–62; permit applicability text lines 21–24
sources.conditions: An offline curb cut at the intended maximum ponding elevation can let excess gutter flow pass once the cell fills. Source distinguishes online flow paths and erosion/short-circuiting concerns.

sources.default: Minnesota recommendations do not establish governing rules for unidentified site
sources.exceptions: Observed bypass at the hypothetical opening is not proof of intended design; recover plans and event context

sources.subject: Curb-cut capture and conditional routing alternatives
sources.operation: EPA Green Streets Handbook February 2021, Ch. 4.4 and design-context note
sources.locator: Printed pp. 4-1, 4-6–4-7; PDF zero-based p45; text lines 1671–1674 and 1878–1963
sources.conditions: Placement in the gutter flow path, grading toward the feature, and steep-slope berm/runnel examples are conditional. Grated cuts and trench drains address specific debris/access situations.
sources.unit: Handbook includes dimensions, but final adopts none

sources.subject: Maintenance, compaction/debris hypotheses, and 48-hour inspection
sources.operation: MPCA O&M page, post-construction schedule and troubleshooting
sources.locator: Independent text lines 101–159 and 225–245; web source post-construction table and common problems
sources.conditions: Later semiannual ponding checks are 48 hours after rain when ground is not frozen; deep sumps may pond. Troubleshooting identifies sediment/clogging as possible, not exclusive, causes. Mulch and debris may obstruct flow.
sources.unit: 48 hours; first-year table includes storms >0.5 inches, not adopted as site event threshold
sources.exceptions: Frozen ground and deep-sump conditions; local design and drain configuration unknown

sources.operation: EPA road/parking-lot runoff O&M technical memorandum, 2016
sources.locator: Printed pp.7–10; text Inspection and Assessment, Infiltration Rates, and records paragraph around lines 328–383, 471–475
sources.conditions: Standing water at 48 hours is an example prompting further evaluation. Inspection cadence depends on drainage area, use/activity and rainfall. Level observations and design/maintenance records support staged assessment.
sources.unit: hour/day observation intervals, not a universal infiltration-rate oracle

sources.subject: Pretreatment selection conditions
sources.operation: Official MPCA article independently retrieved by web tool; direct HTTP body was CAPTCHA
sources.locator: Pretreatment compatibility/applicability and definitions; web lines 91–106, 147–162
sources.conditions: Pretreatment filter strips need shallow distributed sheet flow; concentrated flow is unsuitable for that type. Forebays are associated with channelized flow; screens with leaves/large debris. Space, topography, downstream practice and maintenance matter.
sources.unit: No device size or quantitative removal rating adopted
sources.type: Pretreatment, not a standalone treatment BMP
sources.exceptions: Candidate does not select a device for an unmeasured curb opening

sources.subject: Groundwater/media boundary and inlet-maintenance mechanisms
sources.conditions: Groundwater interaction with media reduces available void space for capture; high seasonal/year-round groundwater is a context for noninfiltration approaches. Inlet guidance addresses grading, damage, grit/leaves/debris.
sources.unit: 2-foot design separation occurs in source but final does not prescribe it
sources.type: National guidance and conditional system boundary
sources.exceptions: No measured groundwater, slow-drawdown diagnosis, local rule or retrofit follows from this passage

sources.subject: Event and antecedent-media-storage study; five-minute method
sources.operation: Independently queried official publisher-indexed article and version notes; direct retrieval blocked
sources.locator: Water 2026 18(18):2320; DOI 10.3390/w18182320; Abstract, §2.1–2.5, §4.1 and Conclusions; indexed methods in web-specific-1.json
sources.conditions: Three wet seasons at two contrasting roof-fed Beijing systems. Storage metrics and response depend on loading, media depth and drainage boundaries. §2.3 explicitly uses 5-minute rainfall records and maximum 30-minute intensity.
sources.unit: 5 min and 30 min method units verified; no performance number adopted
sources.type: Two engineered field cases with different outflow accounting, not a local oracle
sources.default: No prescribed rainfall interval for the hypothetical pilot
sources.exceptions: Index-retrieved primary text verified relevant passage; no full direct article/raw-data audit. Final omission is a reviewer-access qualification, not proof earlier method claim was false.

sources.version: Water 2026, 18(18), 2320; DOI 10.3390/w18182320; publisher Version of Record notes dated 2026-09-16
sources.independence: Reviewer retrieved primary content independently; candidate source identity is used only for cross-navigation. Candidate/reviewer agreement is not proof.
sources.retrieval_limit: Direct publisher HTTP response 403 and web full-page rate-limit; official publisher-indexed abstract/method sections accessed. Section 2.3 independently confirms five-minute weather data and maximum 30-minute intensity. No full-paper/raw-data replication claimed.
